title: Sum of the Numbers That Occur Once

concept.title: Filter by count
body: Counting with a map is often only the first step. Once you know how often each value occurs, you can **filter** the entries by their count and combine the values that remain. Here we keep the values whose count is exactly 1 and add them.
A value that occurs several times is not added at all (not even once). If no value occurs exactly once, the sum is 0.

statement: Add up all the values that occur exactly once in an array of `n` integers. Values that occur more than once are not counted at all. Print the sum (0 if there is no such value).
hints: Count how often each value occurs.
Go through the map and take the values whose count is 1.
Add them; the answer may be 0.
